newsitem.title: UK: Britain breaks off contacts with Sinn Fein.
newsitem.headline: Britain breaks off contacts with Sinn Fein.

text.p: Britain said on Monday it had broken off contacts with Sinn Fein, the political wing of the outlawed Irish Republican Army, after the guerrilla group admitted killing two Northern Ireland policemen in an ambush.
"Following today's murders there is no question of agreeing to meet Sinn Fein," a spokesman for the Northern Ireland Office said in response to an enquiry.
Government officials had held two meetings with Sinn Fein to clarify the conditions under which the party could be admitted to peace talks on the political future of the province.
Northern Ireland Secretary Mo Mowlam said last week she would agree to a third meeting but it would be the last one unless the IRA unequivocally restored the ceasefire it broke in February 1996.

Mowlam described Monday's murder of the two officers, who were shot at close range while on routine patrol near the centre of the busy County Armagh town of Lurgan, as "an appalling outrage". The IRA, using a recognised code word, claimed the killings in a call to a Belfast radio station.
